jobs.title: Clinical Quality Operations Manager- Remote
jobs.description:
Job Description

It is critical that consistent, accurate, high-quality data is generated and maintained from clinical trials conducted worldwide. In collaboration with the Clinical Quality Operations Lead (CQOL) and Head of CQO, the CQOM is responsible for the execution of clinical quality oversight activities within an assigned trial.   This includes proactive quality management, risk-based quality oversight, and clinical trial inspection management activities.

The CQOM will provide clinical quality operations support to Trial Teams (TTs) to proactively embed quality into sponsored trials, ensure robust supplier oversight, and address critical quality issues as needed.
The incumbent will assist with the overall strategy for maintaining ongoing inspection readiness, as well as preparing for, managing, and following up on regulatory inspections.

Core Responsibilities:
Trial Team, Research Portfolio and Enterprise Support
- Independently support assigned Trial Teams (TT) and drive implementation of Quality by Design.
- Act as a Process Subject Matter Expert (SME) within Clinical Quality Operations, providing guidance on quality processes, standards, and regulatory requirements to TTs.
- Support identification, investigation, escalation, and resolution of study-level quality issues including Significant Quality Issues (SQIs) and Serious Breaches (SBs).
- Support Trial Teams in assessing trial health and conducting quality reviews, as needed.
- Lead Inspection Hypercare Teams (IHT) with the aim of ensuring that, at all stages, the Trial Team (TT) maintains ongoing inspection readiness.

Regulatory GCP Inspections & Research and Development Quality Assurance Audits
·       Provide oversight for operational management of sponsor inspections (e.g., act as Control Room Lead or Control Room Support).
·       Act as Inspection Lead for site inspections.
·       Conduct pre-inspection visit (PIV) for impending site inspections.
·       Author key inspection communications (e.g., daily summaries, inspection outcomes, and issue escalations).
·       Coordinate the inspection response process managing the root cause analysis, Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) and associated regulatory commitments to completion, ensuring that key inspection documentation is maintained at all times.
·       Support Quality Assurance audits (i.e., Study Level Audits) providing support to TT before, during and after audit, including coordinating root cause analysis for any applicable observations, development of responses, CAPA management and tracking.

Clinical Quality Risk Management
·       Collaborate with the Clinical Quality Risk Manager (CQRM) to operationalize quality risk management during trial conduct.
·       Provide critical insights from study level audits, inspections, and quality issues and support identification of actionable resolution pathways for quality signals that emerge during trial conduct.

Service Provider Quality Oversight
·       Serve as the primary clinical quality Point of Contact (POC) for assigned key service providers (e.g., tier 1 and tier 2 service providers).
·       Responsible for the strategic development and management of service provider clinical quality agreements.

Mergers & Acquisitions
·       Support quality-related mergers and acquisitions activities, as required, to ensure comprehensive knowledge transfer, risk management, and inspection readiness.

CQO Infrastructure, Process Innovation & Special Projects
·       Contribute to the ongoing development of CQO infrastructure and process innovation.
·       Support and lead special projects and strategic assignments within CQO as assigned by CQOL.

AI Efficiency & Optimization
·       Proactively identify and apply AI-driven approaches to improve operational efficiency and decision-making within CQO.
·        Work with data and analytics to monitor performance and drive continuous improvement.

Qualifications, Skills & Experience

Education
·       Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree or equivalent in a health care or scientific area.

Experience

·       Minimum of 8 years of relevant experience in the pharmaceutical industry and/or clinical research.
·       Robust knowledge of quality management and clinical trial operations.
·       Comprehensive knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS), ICH GCP guidelines, and worldwide Regulatory Health Authority requirements.
·       Advanced experience in independent root cause analysis (RCA), CAPA development and effectiveness management, and service provider quality oversight.

Skills
·       Superior oral and written communication skills in an international, matrixed environment.
·       Excellent project management and organizational skills.
·       Ability to lead cross-functional teams of business and clinical professionals.
·       Able to act urgently and decisively on worldwide health authority inspection matters.
·       Ability to analyze, interpret, and solve complex quality and compliance issues.
. Ability to think strategically and objectively with digital savvy (awareness of AI and machine learning tools)

jobs.title: Executive Director, IT Finance Lead
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Executive Director, IT Finance Lead is a senior IT leadership role responsible for shaping and delivering the global technology strategy for Finance. This leader will serve as a trusted partner to Finance business stakeholders and provide functional and technical leadership across a portfolio of financial systems and solutions supporting enterprise-wide financial processes. The individual is a proactive technology thought leader, strategist, and delivery orchestrator.

This role will be critical to driving the AI transformation of the Finance function, working collaboratively with Finance functional leaders to identify and prioritize high-value opportunities, reimagine business processes, and responsibly scale AI, data, and automation capabilities. The leader will help translate Finance priorities into an integrated technology roadmap that improves decision-making, productivity, business performance, control, and operational efficiency.

The role oversees a team of IT professionals with expertise in financial applications and solutions. The Executive Director will partner closely with business and IT leaders to define roadmaps, modernize the technology landscape, and deliver integrated, end-to-end solutions.

The scope includes global ownership of financial systems and solutions supporting Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A), Tax, Treasury, Account-to-Report and Controller, and Order-to-Cash. The leader will ensure these systems are compliant, secure, modernized, and aligned with enterprise controls and SOX requirements, while advancing innovation through AI, automation, and integrated solutions.

Primary Responsibilities:

Strategic Leadership
- Serve as a trusted strategic partner to Finance functional leaders, translating Finance priorities into an integrated technology, data, AI, and automation strategy.
- Lead the AI transformation of the Finance function, partnering with functional leaders to identify high-value opportunities, reimagine end-to-end processes, and responsibly scale AI-enabled capabilities.
- Shape and maintain the global Finance technology roadmap, balancing business transformation, modernization, operational resilience, compliance, and technical sustainability.
- Establish a value-led approach for prioritizing Finance technology and AI investments, with clear business outcomes, adoption measures, and accountability for value realization.
- Influence the future Finance operating model by bringing external insights, emerging technology perspectives, and innovative solutions to Finance leadership.
- Build strong alignment across Finance, IT, Data, AI, Risk, and other enterprise stakeholders to deliver integrated solutions and avoid fragmented technology investments.
- Provide strategic leadership across the Finance technology portfolio, ensuring priorities remain aligned with enterprise strategy, financial controls, security, and regulatory requirements.
- Develop organizational capabilities and talent needed to support the evolving Finance technology landscape, including AI, data, automation, digital products, and modern financial platforms.

Solution Ownership and Delivery
- Serve as the system/product owner for financial applications within the area of responsibility.
- Ensure applications and platforms remain compliant, secure, modernized, and supported through effective lifecycle management.
- Lead the delivery of IT solutions for Finance from concept through implementation and support.
- Translate business requirements into robust digital solutions and ensure technical teams are aligned to desired functional outcomes.
- Partner with other IT leaders to ensure end-to-end, integrated enterprise solutions across business functions.
- Promote strong operational discipline, documentation, and supportability across all delivered solutions.
- Own the Finance products through its entire lifecycle; sets the product vision, roadmaps, and strategy, ensuring value and user experience are measured and achieved.

Finance Domain Scope
- Oversee technology solutions such as SAP FICO, HANA Sidecar, OneSource tax engine, Wall Street Suite for Treasury, SAP BDC Seamless Planning and others supporting: - Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A)
- Tax
- Treasury
- Account to Report (including Close & Controls management)
- Product costing
- Order-to-Cash

Innovation, AI, and Automation
- Identify and deliver opportunities for AI-enabled capabilities and automation across Finance processes.
- Drive continuous improvement and modernization of the financial application portfolio.
- Champion new technologies and solution patterns that increase efficiency, data quality, and decision making.
- Scans the market for technology solutions that could transform the Finance Digital landscape and experiment with select capabilities that show a lot of promise.

Governance, Controls, and Compliance
- Ensure financial systems and processes align with internal controls, audit expectations, and SOX requirements.
- Partner with compliance, risk, security, and enterprise architecture teams to maintain a strong controls environment.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Territory Sales Manager - Companion Animal
- Permanent full-time role with competitive renumeration, benefits and tools of trade provided e.g. Car, Laptop, ipad etc.

- Location & Territories Covered: Auckland, New Zealand

- TSM role would suit a passionate, motivated sales orientated individual with an interest in Companion Animal Health

- Be part of a trusted global leader in Animal Health with market leading products

- Work with a high performing, agile and passionate sales team

As a Territory Sales Manager - Companion Animal, you will be responsible for maximising sales across the company’s product range within a designated territory. You will develop and execute territory plans, build strong customer relationships and work closely with technical and sales teams to deliver business results.

What You Will Do

Responsibilities include, however not limited to:

Territory Sales and Planning
- Achieve sales targets and activity levels for assigned territory and products

- Develop, implement and regularly review territory plans to support sales achievement

- Analyse customer data to support territory, customer and pre-call planning

- Identify and target high-value customers

Customer Relationship Management
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with customers and clients, including veterinarians, vet nurses, store managers, field representatives, veterinary technicians and business managers

- Leverage strong business relationships to deliver commercial results

- Identify customer needs and clearly communicate how our company’s Animal Health products and services provide solutions

- Articulate the value of our company’s Animal Health products versus other treatment options

- Provide corporate sales presentations to consumer groups, customers and wholesalers as required

Sales Execution and Technical Support
- Identify and participate in promotional tactics to maximise sales

- Utilise the technical services team to support delivery of technical messaging and drive sales

- Provide technical and sales training to wholesalers and customers to ensure accurate messaging reaches the end user

- Maintain a high level of product knowledge, including competitor products and broader animal health issues

- Monitor competitor activity and develop action plans to respond within the territory

- Keep the Regional Sales Manager / Sales Lead informed of competitor activity through regular reporting

CRM, Reporting and Compliance
- Record customer interactions in CRM systems, such as MAXX, to inform next-call objectives and support a single view of the customer

- Ensure product complaint investigations, pricing queries, compliance issues and follow-up requests are completed accurately and within required timelines

- Ensure all business activity complies with relevant Acts, policies and procedures

- Share knowledge, communicate effectively across sales and marketing teams, and contribute positively to team meetings and forums

What You Must Have
- Tertiary business or science degree preferred

- Demonstrated commercial success in a sales role essential

- Strong relationship-building and influencing skills

- Ability to communicate technical information clearly and effectively

- High flexibility, resilience and problem-solving ability

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including presentation skills

- Excellent organisational skills and responsiveness to customer needs

- Ability to work collaboratively and inclusively with others

- Self-starter who works well with minimal supervision

- Intermediate Microsoft Office skills, including Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and comfort using technology such as iPads

- Ability to make day-to-day decisions in line with normal business activities

- Strong negotiation skills and an active interest in improving selling skills, including Action Selling and key account management principles

What You Can Expect
- Play a pivotal role by bringing your  sales talent  to a  market leading  global  Animal Health organisation with  trusted brands  and  innovative products

- Join a  close knit, collaborative team  of  like-minded professionals  who  celebrate wins  and share knowledge

- Competitive salary  with  performance related bonus  and  recognition programmes

- Maximise sales across a leading companion animal product range

Job Description

Grow and accelerate your career with our Oncology Sales organization and join a team that’s driven to make an impact on cancer patients. We take a customer-centric approach by leveraging emerging digital technologies and data analytics to better understand our patients' needs and design ingenious solutions to meet them. As an Oncology Customer Team Leader (District Sales Manager), you will manage and lead a team of Oncology Sales Representatives/Specialists that partner with customers to uncover and address their needs, educate key stakeholders about our oncology products, and communicate our vision to the broader oncology community.

- This is a field-based, sales management role that will be responsible for a team of Oncology Sales Representatives/Specialists for the Northwest District.
- The district covers Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Montana, and Wyoming.

- Coach direct reports, oversee training, and complete people management processes for Oncology Sales professionals.
- Develop and resource their customer team to address customer needs.

- Collaborate with Oncology Sales organization, including Customer Team Leaders, Commercial Operations Directors, Account Managers, and alliance partnerships.

- Communicate and coordinate with both district and cross-functional teams and share best practices with direct reports and peers.

jobs.title: Director Strategic Planning
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Enterprise Strategy Office (ESO) develops, implements, and drives enterprise strategy in support of our company, its customers, and shareholders. The scope of this group includes ​​strategic program management, enterprise strategic planning, risk management, as well as strategic venture investments in healthcare as part of our Global Health Innovation fund. Together, we identify business critical challenges, create, and evaluate options, and ensure effective implementation and cross-functional engagement.

Position Description:

The Director of Commercial Strategy Development will lead and support strategy development for enterprise-critical commercial initiatives, assessing and designing priorities that are complex questions with significant upside for the company, but high ambiguity. This includes ongoing initiatives across our Company as well as the establishment of new strategies and capabilities. This role will work cross-functionally with senior leaders (e.g., Executive Team, ET-1, ET-2) to socialize and refine initiatives, building a coalition of support that is needed to drive the creation of value and adoption of change.
The ideal candidate will possess innovation, insight, commercial acumen, and broad market perspectives to provide commercial strategy expertise for our company. Compelling candidates will have strategic consulting experience, well-rounded capabilities as well as pharmaceutical industry experience. Commercial, marketing, market access and/or analytics experience are particularly valuable for this role.
Reporting to the Executive Director, Commercial Strategy, Enterprise Strategy Office. Located in Rahway, NJ preferred. Candidates from Upper Gwynedd, PA will be considered

Primary Responsibilities:

- Lead and support the development of enterprise critical commercial initiatives. Identifying opportunities, creating evaluations, and recommendations, in collaboration with commercial executive leaders.
- Partner in the implementation of critical commercial priorities that require substantial cross-divisional collaboration, strategic thought-partnership, and negotiation to deliver the best solution and impact for the business.
- Use existing or develop novel strategic frameworks to lay out potential options, evaluate implications and conduct ‘what you need to believe’ or similar analytical analyses to drive to a final recommendation.
- Bring outside-in perspectives, contributing new ideas and priorities to commercial leadership, leveraging experience and depth of understanding of evolving industry trends.
- Collaborate with commercial leaders on prioritized business unit needs and launch planning and excellence providing strategic thought-partnership.
- Partner with commercial and cross-divisional leaders to bring in market and competitive perspectives that inform therapeutic area portfolio strategy (e.g., outside-in commercial assessment for opportunity sizing, target product profile development).
- Manage directly and indirectly internal and external associates dedicated to our programs.
- Create thriving and psychologically safe engagements, leading without authority to provide new and novel strategic perspectives.

Minimum Required Skills:

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent required, Master’s in Business Administration or PhD preferred
- 4+ years of strategy management consulting experience from a top-tier firm (e.g., BCG, McKinsey, L.E.K., ZS, Kearney)
- Minimum of 5+ years of biopharmaceutical experience across diverse roles of increasing responsibility, including commercial experience in US/Global marketing and asset launches required.
- Use existing or develop novel strategic frameworks to lay out potential options, evaluate implications and conduct ‘what you need to believe’ or similar analytical analyses to drive to a final recommendation.
- High business acumen distilling complex commercial problems, create structured framing, assessments, and actionable recommendations in collaboration with commercial colleagues.
- Analytical expertise and external landscape knowledge to build data-driven insights to inform recommendations including experience with, or awareness of, developing commercial market assessments on therapeutic / disease area strategy to inform development of TPP.
- Strong ability to influence decision-making in a highly matrixed organization, demonstrating empathy, collaboration, and high Emotional Intelligence.
- Demonstrated ability to thrive in ambiguity, exceling in bringing cross-functional colleagues together leading high-priority initiatives .
- Ability to prioritize time and problem solve to focus on most impactful initiatives.
- Strong communicator with excellent verbal and written skills; ability to communicate effectively with senior management and across all levels of the business
- Driven, curious, and collaborative professional with a growth mindset, strong organizational skills, and a willingness to learn.

Required Skills:
Adaptability, Adaptability, Analytical Tools, Budget Management, Business Acumen, Business Analysis, Business Decisions, Business Operations, Business Opportunity Identification, Business Planning, Data-Driven Decision Making, Decision Making, Developing Proposals, Enterprise Leadership, Executive Presence, Industry Trend Analysis, Influencing Skills, Management Consulting, Managing Ambiguity, Market Access, Market Research, Oncology Marketing, Organizational Leadership, Pharmaceutical Industry, Results-Oriented {+ 7 more}

jobs.title: Senior Specialist Procurement (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Job Description

Unser Geschäftsbereich Tiergesundheit ist ein vertrauenswürdiger, weltweit führender Anbieter in der Veterinärmedizin. Die Erhaltung und Verbesserung der Gesundheit, des Wohlbefindens und der Leistungsfähigkeit von Tieren und den Menschen, die diese pflegen, stehen dabei im Fokus. Wir sind ein globales Team unterschiedlicher Fachleute, das gemeinsam daran arbeitet, einen positiven Beitrag für die Tierhaltung und die weltweite Nahrungsmittelversorgung zu leisten. Wir haben ein tiefes Verantwortungsbewusstsein gegenüber unseren Kunden, Verbrauchern, Tieren, der Gesellschaft und unserem Planeten.

Als eines der bedeutendsten forschenden Pharmaunternehmen in der Veterinärmedizin bietet Tiergesundheit Tierärzten, Landwirten, Tierhaltern und Regierungen eines der größten Portfolios an Tierarzneimitteln, Impfstoffen, Gesundheitslösungen und Dienstleistungen im Bereich Gesundheitsmanagement sowie eine umfangreiche Palette von digital vernetzten Produkten zur Identifizierung, Rückverfolgbarkeit und Überwachung. Wir investieren in dynamische, umfangreiche Forschungs- und Entwicklungsaktivitäten und eine moderne, globale Lieferkette. Wir sind in mehr als 50 Ländern vertreten. Unsere Produkte sind in rund 150 Märkten erhältlich.

AUFGABEN

- Verantwortung für die indirekte Beschaffung (CAPEX und OPEX); zusätzlich Unterstützung bei der Beschaffung direkter Materialien nach Bedarf, um Versorgungssicherheit, Risikominimierung und die Erreichung der Geschäftsziele zu fördern
- Steuerung des gesamten Beschaffungsprozesses einschließlich Lieferanten- und Angebotsanalyse, Lieferantenauswahl, Verhandlungen, Auftragsausführung und SLA-Vereinbarungen
- Zentrale Ansprechperson für das Lieferantenmanagement
- Erreichen der Kosteneinsparungsziele durch funktionsübergreifende Zusammenarbeit
- Leitung strategischer Sourcing-Projekte und Mitwirkung an Initiativen im Einklang mit den Beschaffungsstrategien des Standorts und der jeweiligen Kategorie
- Steuerung des Lieferantenrisikomanagements und Maßnahmen zur Versorgungssicherheit, einschließlich Risikoidentifikation, Planung von Minderungsmaßnahmen und Nachverfolgung
- Entwicklung und Leitung von Plänen zur Verbesserung der Lieferantenleistung in Zusammenarbeit mit internen Stakeholdern und Lieferanten
- Leitung komplexer, funktionsübergreifender Beschaffungsprojekte sowie Sicherstellung einer wirksamen Abstimmung der Stakeholder und der Erreichung der vereinbarten Ziele
- Unterstützung bei der Überwachung und Berichterstattung wesentlicher Beschaffungs-KPIs und Leistungskennzahlen zur Förderung operativer Exzellenz und kontinuierlicher Verbesserung
- Pflege beschaffungsrelevanter Stamm- und Berichtsdaten, Sicherstellung der Einhaltung der Global-Sourcing-Richtlinien sowie Unterstützung lieferantenbezogener Qualitätssicherungsprozesse

QUALIFIKATIONEN

- Abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium (idealerweise in Betriebswirtschaftslehre oder Chemie/Prozessindustrie) kombiniert mit mehrjähriger Berufserfahrung in der Beschaffung oder gleichwertige Ausbildung und mehrjährige einschlägige Berufserfahrung
- Mindestens 5 Jahre relevante Berufserfahrung in der Beschaffung innerhalb der pharmazeutischen Industrie
- Kaufmännische und administrative Kenntnisse
- Kommunikationskompetenz, Teamfähigkeit, eigenverantwortliches Arbeiten, analytisches Denken und Projektmanagementkompetenz
- Sehr gute Kenntnisse in SAP und ARIBA
- Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit mit Teams im multinationalen Umfeld wünschenswert
- Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

Wir sind stolz darauf, ein Unternehmen zu sein, das auf den Werten seiner vielfältigen, talentierten und engagierten Mitarbeiter aufbaut. Der schnellste Weg innovative Entwicklungen voranzutreiben ist, unterschiedliche Ideen in einer integrativen Umgebung zusammenzubringen. Wir bestärken unsere Kollegen darin, sachlich über ihre Vorstellungen zu diskutieren und Probleme gemeinsam anzupacken. Wir sehen uns als Arbeitgeber der Chancengleichheit und engagieren uns dafür, integrative, vielfältige Arbeitsplätze zu fördern.

jobs.description:
Job Description

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Associate Director, Cluster Commercial Service & Transformation Lead is a critical leadership role for the Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan Cluster. The role will establish and lead a future-ready Commercial Service Center that provides scalable, high-quality, technology-enabled execution support to commercial teams, while accelerating simplification, automation, innovation, and new ways of working.
The incumbent will design and evolve the service operating model, strengthen service governance and performance management, and lead, upskill, and transform a team of 10+ commercial associates, marketing associates, administrative assistants and PMO specialists into a stronger commercial service and execution capability. The role will also serve as the main contact for third-party service partners, ensuring service quality and issue resolution meet business expectations, while driving adoption of digital, AI-enabled, and productivity tools and exploring technology collaboration opportunities that create measurable business, customer, and patient value.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Commercial Service Center Operating Model & Service Delivery
- Design and continuously evolve the Cluster Commercial Service Center operating model, including service scope, service catalog, role clarity, service standards, governance rhythm and ways of working across Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan.
- Lead end-to-end service delivery for core commercial operations support, ensuring execution is timely, compliant, customer-oriented, and focused on enabling commercial teams to spend more time on strategic and customer-facing priorities.
- Act as the primary business owner for internal and third-party service providers, proactively managing service levels, quality standards, issue resolution, and continuous improvement against evolving business needs.
- Establish transparent service performance management, including workload visibility, capacity planning, service quality indicators, stakeholder feedback, and productivity improvement.
- Identify recurring pain points, bottlenecks, duplication, and low-value activities, and convert them into prioritized service improvement and transformation actions.

Simplification, Automation & Technology Adoption
- Build and manage a practical simplification and automation pipeline, prioritizing opportunities based on business value, feasibility, compliance considerations, workload reduction, and stakeholder impact.
- Lead simplification and standardization initiatives across recurring commercial processes, forming cross-functional teams where needed to deliver measurable improvements.
- Translate business pain points into clear process redesign, automation use cases, AI & technology adoption, business requirements, pilots, and scalable operating solutions.
- Partner with Commercial Excellence and DHH Team to implement approved digital, AI-enabled, and productivity solutions into daily business operations.
- Track and communicate transformation benefits, including cycle-time reduction, quality improvement, capacity release, service experience, and adoption progress.

Project Management Officer
- Serve as project management lead for key strategic and operational programs, ensuring clear scope, disciplined execution, proactive risk management, stakeholder alignment, and cross-functional delivery
- Lead one PMO specialist who provides hands-on project management support, including workplan coordination, meeting cadence, milestones, owners, risks, dependencies, and action tracking, documentation, and progress reporting.

Technology Collaboration & Innovation Opportunities
- Systematically scan external healthcare, AI, and technology trends to identify emerging changes, opportunities, and potential implications for Cluster commercial operations and customer engagement.
- Translate external trends and business pain points into practical innovation opportunities, collaboration concepts, pilot proposals, and clear business use cases.
- Build and coordinate internal and external technology collaboration projects where there is clear business relevance, measurable value, and alignment with compliance and company priorities.
- Engage cross-functional stakeholders across Commercial, Medical, Access, Compliance, Legal, IT/Digital, and external partners to shape pilots, define success measures, manage risks, and support implementation.

People Leadership & Capability Building
- Lead, coach, and upskill a team of 10+ commercial associates, marketing associates, administrative assistants and PMO specialists into a stronger commercial service, project execution, and technology-enabled operations capability.
- Redefine team capabilities from task execution toward business coordination, project management, process ownership, stakeholder partnering, and digital/AI-enabled support.
- Build structured development plans across service excellence, stakeholder communication, process excellence, digital and AI fluency, project coordination, compliance awareness, and problem solving.
- Create clear standards for ownership, service mindset, responsiveness, quality, professionalism, continuous improvement, and business partnership.
- Foster an inclusive and motivating team environment during transformation, helping colleagues build confidence, adopt new ways of working, and grow into future-ready commercial operations roles.

WHAT YOU MUST HAVE

- Bachelor’s degree or above in Business Administration, Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Operations Management, Technology, or a related field; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
- 8+ years of experience in commercial operations, service delivery, commercial excellence, transformation, project management, consulting, technology adoption, digital innovation, or related roles.
- Proven experience designing or improving operating models, service delivery processes, governance rhythms, service standards, and stakeholder-facing support models in a complex business environment.
- Demonstrated ability to lead simplification and standardization initiatives, form cross-functional teams where needed, and deliver measurable improvements in speed, quality, productivity, and user experience.
- Strong technology and AI business adoption capability, with proven experience identifying use cases, partnering with digital/technology teams or external collaborators, and embedding digital, automation, or AI-enabled solutions into business operations.
- Ability to scan external healthcare, AI, and technology trends and convert insights into practical innovation opportunities, pilots, collaboration projects, or business use cases.
- Strong project management capabilities.
- Proven people leadership experience, with the ability to coach, upskill, and transform team through changing business expectations.
- Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills.
- Good understanding of pharmaceutical commercial operations, healthcare environment, compliance expectations, customer engagement needs, and business execution requirements.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and storytelling skills, with high ownership, learning agility, and change leadership.
- Fluent in English and Mandarin.

CORE COMPETENCIES

- Service excellence and customer orientation
- Operating model design and execution discipline
- Simplification, automation, and continuous improvement
- Technology and AI agility, with the ability to translate emerging tools into practical business use cases
- Proven ability to drive technology adoption into business operations and build effective internal and external collaborations

jobs.title: Regional Sales Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

Are you an inspiring sales leader passionate about developing high-performing teams and driving commercial excellence in oncology? Join us as Regional Sales Manager, where you will empower your team, build strategic healthcare partnerships, and directly impact the lives of cancer patients across Poland.

Purpose of the Position
In this key leadership role, you will translate national business priorities into impactful regional execution plans, driving sales performance, market share, and customer engagement. You will serve as a strategic regional business leader, coach, and capability builder, ensuring our customer-facing teams deliver differentiated value and improve patient pathways within the Polish oncology ecosystem.

Welcome to Our Team
Reporting directly to the National Sales Director, you will lead and inspire a dedicated regional team of at least six Account Managers and Specialists. We are focused on building a unified, highly collaborative organization that thrives on synergy, diverse perspectives, and shared success. Here, you will find an inclusive, supportive environment focused on continuous learning, talent development, and preparing the next generation of leaders

Main Responsibilities
- Drive Regional Performance: Own regional business results, market share growth, and budget management, balancing short-term objectives with long-term account development.
- Lead & Coach Teams: Lead field sales execution and establish coaching excellence through structured field observations, feedback, and individualized development plans.
- Build Capabilities: Drive the regional capability agenda, helping your team advance their skills in value demonstration, ecosystem vision, and omnichannel engagement.
- Ecosystem & Account Planning: Lead regional stakeholder mapping and integrated account planning, leveraging patient journey insights to improve customer impact.
- KOL & Stakeholder Engagement: Manage relationships with key accounts, scientific leaders, and healthcare decision-makers across the region.
- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Align with Medical, Market Access, Marketing, and Commercial Operations to ensure coordinated customer engagement and resource optimization.
- Resource Allocation: Build regional business cases, conduct territory planning, and allocate resources effectively to maximize impact.
- Develop Future Leaders: Identify talent, build robust succession pipelines, and foster an environment of peer mentoring and accountability.

jobs.title: Associate Director, US Site Payment Operations, Operations Lead
jobs.description:
Job Description

Role Description:

The Associate Director, Site Payment Operations, Operations Lead, reports to the Head, Site Payment Operations and leads U.S. site payment execution within Regional Operations. The role is accountable for day-to-day delivery, controls, workforce coordination, service performance, and the timely containment of operational issues, ensuring that payments to clinical trial sites are accurate, timely, and compliant. Drawing on U.S. execution experience, the role also contributes to the strategic direction of the global site payment process by helping shape global priorities, business rules, controls, functional requirements, and solutions under the direction of the Head, Site Payment Operations. The role partners with Site Budgets & Payments Operational Excellence, regional payment teams, and other functional teams to support a common global payment approach and sustainable process and system improvements.

Primary Responsibilities:

- Lead U.S. site payment execution and translate the global capability direction, business rules, priorities, and controls established by Site Payment Operations into consistent day-to-day operations.
- Own U.S. delivery performance across assigned teams, including payment timeliness and accuracy, backlog management, control execution, capacity, and service outcomes.
- Accountable for the integrity and effectiveness of U.S. payment operations across interconnected systems, including transaction integrity, exception management, reconciliations, and synchronization of payment records.
- Lead, coach, and coordinate payment operations teams by establishing clear accountabilities, workload priorities, performance expectations, and workforce readiness.
- Monitor operational data, service measures, controls, and stakeholder feedback; identify performance variations and take corrective action within the role’s execution authority.
- Maintain clear communication with sites, study teams, Finance, Tax, IT/Technology, and other stakeholders regarding payment timelines, risks, dependencies, and service issues.
- Lead immediate containment, recovery, and stakeholder communication when U.S. payment operations fail or services are disrupted.
- Diagnose execution issues, resolve those within operational control, and document and transition systemic process, policy, data, or technology issues to the appropriate owner for permanent resolution.
- Escalate material risks, recurring failures, capacity constraints, and decisions requiring capability-level direction to the Head, Site Payment Operations; recommend strategic priorities or global changes when U.S. or cross-regional execution experience indicates a broader need.
- Contribute payment subject-matter expertise, execution insights, operational data, and regional perspectives to inform the strategic direction, priorities, business rules, controls, and functional requirements of the global site payment process under the leadership of the Head, Site Payment Operations.
- Partner with Site Budgets & Payments Operational Excellence, regional payment teams, IT/Technology, Finance, Tax, and other stakeholders to evaluate global payment scenarios, shape process and system solutions, support the implementation and operational adoption of approved changes, and validate that solutions work effectively across regional contexts.

Qualifications, Skills & Experience:

Required Education:

- A minimum of a Bachelor’s Degree is required (scientific, business, or related discipline preferred); an advanced degree is a plus.

Required Experience and Skills:

- A minimum of five (5) years of clinical research experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, including experience in site payments, clinical trial financial operations, or related operations.
- Experience with investigator payments, clinical trial financial operations, payment systems, controls, or related financial processes.
- Demonstrated ability to lead operational teams, manage capacity and performance, develop talent, and deliver reliable service outcomes in a matrixed organization.
- Ability to translate operational needs into clear business rules, functional requirements, controls, acceptance criteria, and consistent team practices.
- Sound judgment in assessing payment risk and operational impact, leading immediate containment and recovery, and escalating systemic issues appropriately.
- Ability to use data, operational insight, and stakeholder feedback to manage priorities, improve performance, and support sound decisions.
- Strong communication and influencing skills, including the ability to explain complex issues and work effectively across functions, systems, and geographies.
- Knowledge of GCP/ICH, applicable regulatory requirements, Fair Market Value principles, and compliant clinical trial payment practices.
- Supports responsible digital, data-driven, and AI-enabled ways of working.

jobs.title: Clinical Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

Clinical Operations Manager

Brief Description of Position
This role is accountable for performance and compliance for assigned protocols in a country in compliance with ICH/GCP and country regulations, internal policies and procedures, quality standards and adverse event reporting requirements internally and externally.
Under the oversight of the Sr. COM, Head COMs or CRD, the person is responsible for budget/finance aspects, for execution and oversight of clinical trial country submissions and approvals and to ensure Site Ready.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
• Ownership of country and site budgets. Development, negotiation and completion of Clinical Trial Research Agreements (CTRA).
• Oversees and tracks clinical research-related payments. Payment reconciliation at study close-out. Oversees FCPA, DPS/OFAC, and maintenance of financial systems. Financial forecasting in conjunction with Sr.COM /other roles.
• Executes and oversees clinical trial country submissions and approvals for assigned protocols.
• Develops local language materials including local language Informed Consents and translations. Interacts with IRB/IEC and Regulatory Authority for assigned protocols.
• Manages country deliverables, timelines and results for assigned protocols to meet country commitments. Responsible for quality and compliance in assigned protocols in country.
• Contributes to the development of local SOPs. Oversees CTCs as applicable.
• Coordinates and liaises with CRM, CTC, CRA, (Finance and Legal if appropriate) to ensure country deliverables are obtained for submissions, budgets, CTRAs and local milestones. Collaborates closely with Headquarter to align country timelines for assigned protocols.
• Provide support and oversight to local vendors as applicable.
• Oversees and coordinates local processes, clinical and ancillary supplies management, importing and exporting requirements, supplies destruction, local electronic/hard copy filing, archiving and retention requirements, and insurance process management. Enters and updates country information in clinical and finance systems.
• Ownership of local regulatory and financial compliance. The position has a significant impact on how a country can deliver country-specific trial commitments and objectives especially during study start-up.
• Required to in/directly influence investigators, external partners and country operations and adheres to budget targets and agreed payment timelines.
• Works in partnership internally with GCTO country operations, finance, regulatory affairs, pharmacovigilance, legal and regional operations, HQ functional areas and externally with vendors and sites, IRB/IECs and Regulatory Authorities in submission and approval related-interactions. Through continual interaction with local clinical team/s successfully delivers clinical and financial contracts within fair market value.
• Contribute or lead initiatives and projects adding value to the business, as appropriate/required.
• Contributes strongly to COM team and other Country Operations roles knowledge by acting as process Subject Matter Expert (SME), sharing best practices, making recommendations for continuous improvement and providing training as appropriate/required.
• Contributes to COM team knowledge by acting as buddy/mentor and sharing best practices as appropriate/required.

Qualifications, Skills & Experience
Core competencies:
• Expertise of core clinical systems, tools and metrics
• Excellent verbal and written influrencing and training/mentoring skills, in local language and English
• Strong coordination and organizational skills
• Skilled knowledge of budget and contract negotiations, local regulatory environment and submission and approval processes, and understanding of how these impact study start-up.
• Ability to indirectly influence investigators, vendors, external partners and country managers to address and resolve issues, with minimal support from the Sr.COM or manager.
• Ability to make decisions independently with limited oversight from Sr.COM or manager.
• Requires strong understanding of local regulatory environment
• Ability to proactively develop risk management and mitigation plans in the country and resolve issues locally.
• Ability to lead a team of CTCs as applicable

Behavioural Competency Expectations:
• Problem solving is essential to this position. Requires the ability to pro-actively identify issues and risks, analyse root cause, and propose solutions to problems and escalate to management as applicable. Specific examples of common problems include: 1) Issues in budget / CTRA negotiations, 2) Quality and compliance issues, 3) Regulatory and legal issues, and 4) issues related to functional area deliverables that could jeopardize protocol milestones.
• Effective and efficient time management, organizational and interpersonal skills, conflict management and problem-solving skills.
• High sense of accountability and urgency in order to properly prioritize deliverables
• Strong communication, leadership, and negotiation skills as well as excellent influencing and training/mentoring skills, both written and verbal, in local language and English.
• Ability to focus on multiple deliverables and protocols simultaneously is essential. Requires that the individual has ability to work effectively also in a remote virtual environment with a wide range of people.
• Positive mindset, growth mindset, capable of working independently and being self-driven
• Able to directly influence site staff

Experience Requirements:
5 years of experience in clinical research or combined experience in Clinical Research and Finance/Business

Educational Requirements:
Bachelor's Degree in Business Finance/ Administration/ Life Science or equivalent Health Care related experience

jobs.title: (Associate) Clinical Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

Join our company, a premier research-intensive biopharmaceutical company, at the forefront of delivering innovative health solutions. We are dedicated to advancing the prevention and treatment of diseases in people and animals. As an (Associate) Clinical Operations Manager, you will play a crucial role in managing clinical trials and ensuring compliance with regulatory standards. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to our mission of using leading-edge science to save and improve lives around the world.

Your Key Contributions
- You'll take ownership of country and site budgets, developing, negotiating, and completing Clinical Trial Research Agreements (CTRA).
- Oversee and track all clinical research-related payments.
- You'll execute and oversee clinical trial country submissions and approvals for assigned protocols.
- Manage country deliverables, timelines, and results to meet our commitments.
- Ensure top-notch quality and compliance in all assigned protocols within the country.
- Contribute to the development of local Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and oversee Clinical Trial Coordinators (CTCs) as needed.
- You'll coordinate and liaise with Clinical Research Managers (CRM), CTCs, Clinical Research Associates (CRA), and other departments to ensure country deliverables are achieved.
- Collaborate closely with Headquarters to align country timelines for protocols.
- Provide support and oversight to local vendors where applicable.
- You'll manage local processes including supply management, importing/exporting, supplies destruction, filing, archiving, retention requirements, and insurance process management.
- Enter and update country information in clinical and finance systems.
- Work internally with various departments such as GCTO country operations, finance, regulatory affairs, and externally with vendors, sites, and regulatory authorities for submission and approval-related interactions.
- Deliver clinical and financial contracts within fair market value through continuous interaction with local clinical teams.

What You Bring to the Table
Required
- You have a Bachelor's Degree in Business Finance/ Administration/ Life Science or equivalent Health Care related experience.
- Minimum of 2-3 years of hands-on experience in clinical research or combined experience in Clinical Research and Finance/Business.
- Experience in regulatory or finance functions.
- You possess strong problem-solving skills with the ability to proactively identify issues and risks, analyze root causes, and propose effective solutions.
- Effective time management, organizational and interpersonal skills, conflict management, and problem-solving skills.
- A high sense of accountability and urgency to properly prioritize deliverables.
- Your communication, leadership, and negotiation skills are exceptional.
- Excellent influencing and training/mentoring skills, both written and verbal, in local language and English.
- Ability to juggle multiple deliverables and protocols simultaneously with ease.

Preferred
- Additional experience in both regulatory and finance functions is considered a strong advantage.

Please note that there are three open vacancies for this role.

jobs.title: Clinical Operations Manager Finance, Remote
jobs.description:
Job Description

This role is accountable for performance and compliance for assigned protocols in a country in compliance with International Council for Harmonisation (ICH)/Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and country regulations, our company's policies and procedures, quality standards and adverse event reporting requirements internally and externally. Under the oversight of the Sr. Clinical Operations Manager (COM), Head COMs or Therapy Area Heads (TAH), the person is responsible for preparing, analyzing, negotiating, and revising Clinical Research related contracts and budgets through all phases of the contract cycle.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
- Prepare, analyze, negotiate, and execute required site agreements and associated budgets including Clinical Trial Research Agreements (CTRA), Master Clinical Trial Research Agreements (MCTRA), Confidentiality Disclosure Agreements (CDA), Multiple Confidentiality Disclosure Agreements (MCDA), Imaging Research Allocation Grid (IRAG), Master Fee Schedules (MFS), Facility Use Agreement (FUA), Reimbursement Letters, Amendments and Assignments
- Utilize legal fallback language, budget parameters, and escalate site-specific issues that do not comply with established guidelines for review and approval
- Maintain database and files for all contracts, approvals, and budgets in conformity with uniform naming and savings convention
- Assume responsibility for all aspects of document and metric tracking to ensure timely execution of site agreements
- Perform quality control checks of agreements prior to execution
- Coordinate and liaise with Clinical Research Manager (CRM), Clinical Trial Coordinator (CTC), Clinical Research Associate (CRA), Clinical Operations Manager - Regulatory (COM-R) (Finance and legal if, appropriate) to collaborate on Site Ready Deliverables including identifying risks and implementing mitigation plans to meet country deliverable timelines and commitments
- Lead and develop relationships with key investigational sites and Site Management Organizations across the contracting and budgeting interface
- Contribute to the development of local Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
- Review, negotiate, escalate, and facilitate business approval for Site Access Forms, Electronic Medical Record (EMR) Access Forms, and Institution Policies as required and applicable
- Liaison with Payment Coordinators / Clinical Trial Coordinator - Finance (CTC-Fs) to issues contingency approvals, troubleshoot, and amend Agreements as required.
- Contribute or lead initiatives and projects adding value to the business, as appropriate/required
- Contribute strongly to COM team and other Country Operations roles knowledge by acting as process Subject Matter Expert (SME), sharing best practices, making recommendations for continuous improvement, and providing training as appropriate/required
- Contribute to COM team knowledge by acting as buddy/mentor and sharing best practices as appropriate/required
- Required to in/directly influence investigators, external partners and country operations to successfully delivers clinical and financial contracts within fair market value
- Works in partnership internally with GCTO (Global Clinical Trial Operations) country operations, finance, regulatory affairs, pharmacovigilance, legal and regional operations, Headquarters (HQ) functional areas and externally with vendors and sites

Core competencies:
- Expertise of core clinical systems, tools and metrics
- Excellent verbal and written influencing and training/mentoring skills, in local language and English
- Strong coordination and organizational skills
- Skilled knowledge of budget and contract negotiation and understanding of how these impact study start-up
- Ability to indirectly influence investigators, vendors, external partners and country managers to address and resolve issues, with minimal support from the Sr.COM or manager
- Ability to make decisions independently with limited oversight from Sr.COM or manager
- Ability to proactively develop risk management and mitigation plans in the country and resolve issues locally
- Ability to lead a team of CTCs as applicable

Behavioral Competency Expectations:
- Problem solving is essential to this position
- Requires the ability to pro-actively identify issues and risks, analyze root cause, and propose solutions to problems and escalate to management as applicable - Specific examples of common problems include: - 1) Issues in budget / Clinical Trial Research Agreement (CTRA) negotiations
- 2) Quality and compliance issues
- 3) Regulatory and legal issues
- 4) issues related to functional area deliverables that could jeopardize protocol milestones

- Effective and efficient time management, organizational and interpersonal skills, conflict management and problem-solving skills
- High sense of accountability and urgency in order to properly prioritize deliverables
- Strong communication, leadership, and negotiation skills as well as excellent influencing and training/mentoring skills, both written and verbal, in local language and English
- Ability to focus on multiple deliverables and protocols simultaneously is essential. Requires that the individual has ability to work effectively also in a remote virtual environment with a wide range of people
- Positive mindset, growth mindset, capable of working independently and being self-driven
- Able to directly influence site staff

Education and Experience Requirements :
- Bachelor's Degree or higher
- 3+ years of experience in negotiating contracts or budgets
- Juris Doctor (JD) degree (preferred)

- Work collaboratively to drive a safe and compliant culture in Carlow.

Job Description:

For over 130 years, we have pioneered groundbreaking science.  Today, we are driven by continuous innovation to develop breakthrough medicines, vaccines and technology.  Rooted in direct experience on the farm and in the clinic, we work hand in hand with our customers every step of the way.

Our singular focus is to empower those who care for animals, helping them manage their vital responsibility with confidence.  Because when it comes to animal health, no one sees it like we do.

Our Company's Animal Health group in Millsboro, DE is a Bio-Technology Center of Excellence that performs vaccine production operations from antigen production through formulation, filling and packaging.

With expertise in mammalian, insect and avian cell culture production (anchorage & non-anchorage dependent), live bird vaccine production, embryonated egg vaccine production, roller bottle vaccine production, bioreactor vaccine production and downstream processing (water in oil emulsions, aseptic filling, lyophilization, etc.), the Millsboro site supplies and supports products for a wide range of species including poultry, equine, swine, bovine and companion animal.

This position is responsible for managing materials entering the manufacturing area and waste exiting. The position also includes responsibilities overseeing the preparation, usage and storage of sterile tanks. The area manager ensures all schedules are met while following all safety and standard operating procedures to meet company product quality standards.

- Review and revise processes and procedures against corporate and regulatory requirements to insure compliance

- Provide training, coordinate problem solving issues with third party

- Ensure proper safety procedures, standard operation procedures and aseptic techniques are followed
- Review current practices and ensure employees meet or exceed current procedures and techniques
- Coordinate Systems Applications and Products (SAP) and database entry and the movement of finished goods and in-process products between facilities
- Including inventory movement and production key performance indicators
- Other duties as assigned, such as scheduling equipment maintenance, various trouble shooting and contribute as needed on cross-functional teams

jobs.title: Associate Director, Governance Risk and Compliance for Data, Data Products and Digital Solutions
jobs.description:
Job Description

We aspire to be the premier research-intensive biopharmaceutical company. At our company, we are at the forefront of research to deliver innovative health solutions that advance the prevention and treatment of diseases in people and animals. We use the power of leading-edge science to save and improve lives around the world. Join us in our mission to promote transparency, accountability, and ethical use of data and AI.

The Associate Director, Governance Risk and Compliance for Data, Data Products and Digital Solutions will lead the development and implementation of governance, compliance, privacy, and responsible AI practices across data, data products, and digital solutions. This role partners with cross-functional teams to embed practical controls and standards throughout the data and AI lifecycle, ensuring solutions are developed and used in alignment with company policies, enterprise standards, and applicable regulations. The position supports the operationalization of data governance frameworks, AI stewardship, privacy-by-design principles, and risk management processes that promote transparency, accountability, and ethical use of data and AI.

jobs.title: Trade Compliance Specialist
jobs.description:
Job Description

An amazing opportunity has arisen for a Trade Compliance Specialist . You will assume the duty to ensure compliance to Internal and External Trade Compliance controls, to maintain the site’s Trade Compliance posture. As the Trade Compliance Specialist, you will interact with the company’s appointed Freight Forwarders and Customs Brokers, Air Cargo Security, Global Trade Compliance, and DGSA specialists, liaise with the OTC COMET Process Steward for purpose of aligning with Trade Compliance, have the opportunity to partner with talented and dedicated colleagues while developing and expanding your career.

What you will do:
Bring energy, knowledge, innovation and leadership to carry out the following:

Revenue
- Obtain Binding Tariff Information for all new materials used on site, and ensure they are used correctly on all import/exports and used by customs clearance agents.
- Leverage Inward Processing Agreement for new materials to obtain favorable duties on imports.
- Submit monthly Bill of Discharge to Revenue Commissioners to demonstrate compliance.
- Retain Authorized Economic Operator status for site to enable swift customs clearance (requires monthly reports and regular audits).
- Provide customs clearance instructions to our Customs Brokers
- Monthly Intrastat & VIES reports to Irish Revenue, TAN account returns for any duties payable.
- Act as the our company's Ireland point of contact for the Irish Exporters Association.
-

Logistics
- Manage Freight budget ($500k). Identify monthly freight costs for incoming shipments related to CMOs selling through intercompany and arrange cross-charge to product cost.
- Support the Transport Management System for all site road freight and act as back-up to Logistics Specialist role

Compliance
- REACH compliance for chemicals imported from outside EU.
- Maintain compliance with Dangerous Goods transportation requirements
- Manage and own site’s compliance with Air Cargo Security requirements.
- Responsible for preparing and submitting Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) reports and related filings to Revenue, ensuring timely, accurate compliance with CBAM obligations.

COMET Process Steward (OTC) back-up role:
- Support the use of COMET as used within the business area represented by the Process Steward and aligned with Global Trade Compliance policy
- Act as Business Role Approver for local (to site) workstream specific roles being granted via the SAP GRC Access Management System.
- Ensures the represented business area engages with the COMET Material Data Steward in support of additions/changes to SAP Material Master Data as appropriate for the area represented.

- Undertake other duties and responsibilities as required to support the team and organisation.

What skills you will need:
In order to excel in this role, you will have:
- A minimum of 5 years of Supply Chain, Logistics and Trade Compliance experience, within the Pharma Industry.
- Certificate in Customs Compliance and Trade Facilitation
- Knowledge of international shipping procedures and customs procedures.
- ADR/IATA/IMO/IMDG regulations for Dangerous goods and Safety regulations
- Known Consignor Certification
- DGSA Certification desirable
- Our Manufacturing Division/Logistics Operational Policies and Procedures
- Experience working with Direct Materials, API and Finished Products
- Knowledge of Trade Compliance related business processes
- Experience working with Revenue.
- GMP Policies and Procedures
- Communication skills are a key element of this position
- Demonstrate strong skill of stakeholder engagement and coordination
- Supply Chain Accreditations desirable

We keep the patient at the very heart of all that we do and strive to find solutions and treatments for some of the world’s most challenging healthcare needs.

We are proud to be a company that embraces the value of bringing diverse, talented, and committed people together. The fastest way to breakthrough innovation is when diverse ideas come together in an inclusive environment.

So, if you are ready to:
Invent solutions to meet unmet healthcare needs, Impact the future by driving one of the world’s leading healthcare companies, and inspire your team to reach their full potential and push the boundaries of science and technology, please apply today
